answers.answer: Select players + 1 Factory cards face-down and return others unseen; put tokens on 11 marked territories; randomly select one structure bonus tile face-up below Popularity Track. Lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.

Character starts at home base; two workers on the two land-adjoined adjoining territories; four mechs on Faction Mat abilities; six stars by faction emblem; six tech cubes in marked green boxes; structures/recruits in matching Player Mat spaces; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; action token ready beside mat. Faction Mat sets power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets popularity, coins and two objectives.

You may take either, both, or neither action, but must move token to a different section; Rusviet may repeat a section, otherwise not. Top gains can pay bottom cost; bottom first is forbidden. Pay all exposed red costs first; choose as much or little green benefit as desired. Mat/upgrades determine exact costs/benefits.

An enemy worker on your structure territory controls it and its resources. Enemy units cannot use your structure abilities; you retain those abilities even without control, except Mill cannot produce if uncontrolled. Spend resources from any territories you currently control, even for an action elsewhere.

No: normal Move selects up to two different units, one adjacent territory each. A carried worker may subsequently move itself. All units may carry any number of resources; only mechs may carry your workers, never your character.

A Speed mech entering enemy-workers-only territory stops and cannot move again that turn; enemy workers immediately retreat home, leaving resources, and you lose one popularity per worker, even if at zero (loss cannot prevent retreat). Your workers cannot independently enter while enemy workers control it.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: Enemy workers only; Speed.

answers.answer: After all units finish the Move action, resolve combats before the bottom action; attacker chooses order of multiple combats. Workers cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.

Bolster costs $1 for two power or one combat card; if draw deck empty, shuffle discards; if both empty draw none. Trade costs $1 for two resources or one popularity; traded resources go to a controlled territory with at least one worker. Cannot Trade resources if all workers are home.

Pay all exposed Produce costs before production; select up to two different controlled territories (plus Mill bonus if controlled); each worker there may produce one terrain-matching token. New workers come left-to-right from Player Mat and go in producing village. You may decline any/all production. New exposed costs apply to future Produce actions, not cost already paid.

Upgrade costs exposed number of oil tokens; move a cube to an empty bracketed red box, improving top benefit/reducing bottom cost. Deploy costs exposed number of metal tokens; place a mech on controlled territory with your worker, never lake; its ability applies to character and all mechs, not workers. Mat and upgrades vary exact amounts. Even after all pieces completed, may pay bottom action for coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.

Build on a controlled territory with your worker; one structure total per territory; Factory allowed, lake/home base forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. Mill works only while controlled; Mine remains your personal tunnel for movement even when enemy-controlled.
answers.evidence: Build; Control, resources and home bases.

answers.answer: Put recruit permanently on any open one-time bonus on Faction Mat; immediately get two power, coins, popularity, or combat cards. Ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where recruit was removed. For active player then left then right; two-player opponent triggers once, not twice; stop if sixth star ends game.

Both secretly select dial 0 to min(7,current power), and optionally one card per participating character/mech; Rusviet People’s Army adds one card if workers present; workers alone never fight. Combat abilities: attacker then defender. Reveal simultaneously; add values, attacker wins ties. Both pay dial power; played cards discarded face-up, card values do not cost track power.

Winner controls territory/resources; losing characters, mechs and workers retreat home, leaving all resources (Nordic Seaworthy may retreat eligible units/workers to adjacent lakes). Winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat; defender loses none; Polania Camaraderie exception applies. Non-Saxony winner gets combat star with 0–1 combat stars, none with 2; Saxony places one after each victory while tokens available. Loser draws one card if revealed any dial power or card power; zero-total loser draws none.

After Move action and all combats, if character remains at encounter, discard token and draw; if loses contested entry, retreats and token stays. Gains go to encounter territory. No additional normal action costs or mat/recruit bonuses apply.

Each player’s character takes one Factory card on its first finish of a Move action there, after combat; chooses from remaining cards and returns rest. One permanent card per player; later visits cannot take/change. Factory card is fifth action section with usual optional top-then-bottom; similar actions grant no mat coins, structure or recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to 2 territories, or 3 for Speed character/mech, with normal restrictions.

Only on own turn before or after completing top/bottom action; may wait but meet all requirements when revealing. Place star and put both objective cards bottom of deck. Normally one objective star; Saxony retains second card and may score both.

Stars for six upgrades, four mechs, four structures, four recruits, all eight workers on board, one revealed objective, combat victory (up to two), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Goals once except combat two and Saxony exception; opponents’ stars do not block. Stars permanent; sixth star immediately ends game.

For bottom-row sixth star, collect primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit before star placement. Then active player first, left neighbor, right neighbor; check game end at each step. If sixth star ends game, pending intermingled battle movement is undone and no further combat; no later neighbor recruit star/bonus resolves.

At 10 popularity use 7–12 tier: 5 stars = $20; 4 other territories plus Factory count 7 (= $21); 13 resources make 6 pairs (= $12), so add $53 to held coins, plus selected structure tile bonus. Ties: workers+mechs+structures, power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune: table, structure eligibility, tiebreaks.

answers.answer: Home base is not a territory. Normally cannot move into any home base, build/deploy there; setup, forced retreats and Crimea unlocked Wayfare exceptions. Expansion bases without matching core factions are inactive.
Mountain metal; tundra oil; farm food; forest wood; village worker; lake/factory nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.

All units can pick up/carry/drop resources mid-movement; mechs can also carry your workers, never character. Speed gives each selected character/mech one extra territory; tunnel jump costs one step and extra step may be before/after; mech can pick up/drop mid-movement. Stops for enemy units/encounters override Speed.
Yes, any unit can enter enemy-structure-only territory and take control without combat. All printed tunnels are adjacent for movement by any unit.
Take a dead turn: move token to a different section and take neither action; never pay partial cost. After Move, choose another section.

Armory adds one power on Trade; Monument one popularity on Bolster. These are built structure benefits on those future actions. You retain abilities even without control, except Mill production; enemy units do not gain your structure abilities.

Riverwalk for character/all mechs (not workers): Nordic/Saxony forests and mountains; Rusviet farms/villages; Crimea farms/tundra; Polania villages/mountains. Nordic Swim lets workers cross rivers to land, not lakes; separate from Riverwalk and does not grant mechs Swim.
Saxony Underpass: controlled mountains and all tunnels (including own Mine) adjacent. Rusviet Township: controlled villages and Factory adjacent. Both are character/mech Move abilities.

Saxony Disarm before combat on a tunnel or own Mine: opponent loses two power on track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery before combat pays one power to reduce opponent power by two, once per combat.
Two mechs plus three workers allow three cards total under People’s Army; requires a character/mech participating. Workers alone never fight.

Crimea Wayfare moves character/mechs from territory or home base to own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases; cannot enter active opponent base.
Crimea Scout steals one random opponent combat card into hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion once per turn spends one card as any one resource regardless of card value.

Nordic Seaworthy character/mechs move to/from lakes and may retreat to adjacent lake; mechs may carry workers. Polania Submerge character/mechs move to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake; no Nordic adjacent-lake retreat exception. Workers on lakes need mech to leave; cannot leave carried workers or resources behind when carrier leaves.

Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after Polania wins combat as aggressor on its turn. Does not protect loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.
Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; first gain may pay second cost.
Character stops and cannot move again that turn upon entering encounter during Factory Move. Encounter resolves after whole Move and all combats, if character remains.

Combat hand count public, but during combat may conceal whether any cards committed until reveal; contents secret until revealed. Objective contents secret until reveal completed. Coins are not hidden, but exact total need not be disclosed on request.

Coins only tangible items exchangeable; agreements informal and unenforceable (tournament even forbids coin exchange for deals). Payment cannot cancel combat initiated by moving onto opposing units; fight after Move; bribes may influence outcome.
Popularity 0–6: $3/star, $2/territory, $1/resource pair; 7–12: $4/$3/$2; 13–18: $5/$4/$3. Controlled lakes count; home bases do not. Only complete resource pairs score; leftover single ignored.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table and territory/resource rules.

answers.answer: Count unique printed tunnels/lakes/encounter locations adjacent to structures; duplicates count once. Tunnels excludes Mines; encounter location counts even token removed. Rivers do not break adjacency. Payout for 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6 (tunnels) or 6–7 (lakes/encounters)=$9; zero=$0.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus eligibility table and notes.

answers.answer: Structures on printed tunnel territories (not Mines): 1=$2, 2=$4, 3–4=$6. Longest continuous straight row; rivers do not break line: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9. Combined structures on farms/tundras: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9.
Yes. Winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by defeated mech on lake.
Popularity star is permanent, but current popularity determines final scoring tier. Other players’ stars never block a goal, so two factions may score same achievement.

Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in clockwise board order Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. Seating matters because ongoing recruit bonuses trigger for immediate left/right neighbors.

River is a border between two land territories; lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. Lake-capable unit may enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
Encounter card is shown to all when drawn, artwork shown, capitalized thematic text read aloud; need not read every option aloud.
No limit on friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
Next clockwise player may begin when current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while current player decides which upgrade/mech/structure/recruit to gain.
No. Top and bottom actions each limited once within a turn, including Rusviet; Rusviet only waives prior-section restriction.
Normal Move may instead gain $1.
No. Workers never return to Player Mat, including after retreat.
Yes, may attack with zero power and/or zero popularity.
Yes. May still fight after combat-star limit; non-Saxony with two stars places no further combat star.
Without Meander, must choose one affordable option; cannot decline to choose; unaffordable coin/popularity options cannot be selected. May take as little of chosen benefit as desired.
No turn-order selection requirement stated; both simultaneously and secretly choose dials/cards, then reveal simultaneously.
Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.
Star goals are awarded as soon as achieved; cannot decline/delay placing star. Completed objective may be held and revealed later, but only on own turn and while requirements all met.
No. Units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes; faction/mech abilities provide exceptions.
No. Recruit stays permanently on chosen one-time bonus and cannot later move.
No. Only character triggers encounter.

Controlled Mill adds one bonus territory to current allowance: 2→up to 3, upgraded 3→up to 4. Mill itself counts as one producing worker and produces terrain token even with no actual worker; each actual worker there also produces normally.
Control is a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not preserve control after last unit leaves and no structure.
Build uses wood; Enlist uses food.
